items.title: Full and observed data under a missingness pattern
items.statement: Let $W=(W_1,\ldots,W_k)$ be a finite vector of full-data components and let $R$ be a finite observation-pattern variable. For each pattern $r$, define the observed projection $W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r)$ and the observed record $O=(R,W_{\mathrm{obs}}(R))$ in the disjoint union of the pattern-specific observed spaces. Missing components remain components of $W$; they are not replaced by numeric zeros.

references.title: Lu Mao, Missing Data: Foundations and Methods, Chapter 1, §§1.1–1.2
National Research Council, The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials, Chapter 4, pp. 47–51

items.title: MCAR, MAR, and MNAR relative to an observation pattern
items.statement: For a supplied response kernel $g(r\mid w)$, MCAR means each pattern probability is constant in the full data; MAR means each pattern probability depends on $w$ only through $W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r)$; and MNAR means that MAR fails for at least one pattern relative to this declared full-data/observed-data partition. MCAR is a special case of MAR.

references.title: Lu Mao, Missing Data: Foundations and Methods, Chapter 1, §§1.3–1.5
National Research Council, The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials, Chapter 4, pp. 50–52

items.title: Observed-data likelihood under a response model
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $W=(W_1,\ldots,W_k)$ have a full-data model dominated by a
common sigma-finite positive measure $\mu$ on the finite product measurable
space $\mathcal W=\prod_{j=1}^k\mathcal W_j$, with selected finite-valued
density representatives $p_\theta$ as in
[[def-dominated-statistical-experiment]] and [[def-likelihood-density]]. Let
$\mathcal R$ be a nonempty finite pattern set, let $I_r$ and $J_r$ be the
observed and missing coordinate sets for pattern $r$, and write
$\pi_r(w)=W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r)$ for its measurable coordinate projection. Let
$g_\psi(r\mid w)$ be a supplied response probability kernel as in
[[def-mcar-mar-and-mnar]], and define the joint model by
$$P_{\theta,\psi}(dw,\{r\})=g_\psi(r\mid w)P_\theta(dw).$$

Fix a finite positive measure $\rho$ equivalent to $\mu$; such a measure
exists for every sigma-finite $\mu$. For each pattern put
$$\kappa_r(B)=\rho(\pi_r^{-1}(B))$$
for measurable $B\subseteq\mathcal W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r)$, and define the finite
measure on the observed disjoint union by
$$\lambda_O(A)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\kappa_r(\{x:(r,x)\in A\}).$$
The full-data marginal law of $W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r)$ and the pattern-$r$
observed sublaw $B\mapsto P_{\theta,\psi}(R=r,\pi_r(W)\in B)$ are absolutely
continuous with respect to $\kappa_r$. Choose finite-valued nonnegative
Radon--Nikodym density representatives $q_{\theta,r}$ and
$\ell_{\theta,\psi,r}$ for these measures. Then the observed record
$O=(R,W_{\mathrm{obs}}(R))$ is dominated by $\lambda_O$ and has density
$\ell_{\theta,\psi}(r,x)=\ell_{\theta,\psi,r}(x)$ at $(r,x)$.

In the product-reference special case where
$\mu=\nu=\bigotimes_{j=1}^k\nu_j$, each $\nu_j$ is sigma-finite, and the
coordinate reordering $w=(x,z)=(W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r),W_{\mathrm{mis}}(r))$
identifies $\nu$ with
$\nu_r^{\mathrm{obs}}\times\nu_r^{\mathrm{mis}}$, where
$\nu_r^{\mathrm{obs}}=\bigotimes_{j\in I_r}\nu_j$ and
$\nu_r^{\mathrm{mis}}=\bigotimes_{j\in J_r}\nu_j$, one may instead use the
pattern reference $\nu_r^{\mathrm{obs}}$, with disjoint-union reference
$\lambda_O^{\mathrm{prod}}(A)=\sum_r\nu_r^{\mathrm{obs}}(\{x:(r,x)\in A\})$.
The observed record is dominated by this sigma-finite measure, and Tonelli's
theorem gives the density versions
$$\bar q_{\theta,r}(x)=\int p_\theta(x,z)\,\nu_r^{\mathrm{mis}}(dz),\qquad
\ell_{\theta,\psi,r}(x)=\int p_\theta(x,z)g_\psi(r\mid x,z)\,\nu_r^{\mathrm{mis}}(dz).$$
An empty coordinate block is a one-point space with unit mass.

references.title: Lu Mao, Missing Data: Foundations and Methods, Chapter 1, §1.2
National Research Council, The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials, Chapter 4, pp. 60–61

items.title: Exact binary-outcome bounds under unrestricted missingness
items.statement:
Let $Y,R\in\{0,1\}$, with $R=1$ meaning that $Y$ is observed, and encode the
observed record as $O=(R,RY)$. When $R=0$, the zero in the second recorded
coordinate is a placeholder and does not assign the missing full-data value
$Y=0$. Put
$$a=P(R=1),\qquad b=P(R=1,Y=1),\qquad 0\le b\le a\le1.$$
Let $\Theta_{a,b}$ be the set of all joint laws $P$ of $(Y,R)$ with these
values of $a$ and $b$, and let the statistical model map $P\in\Theta_{a,b}$
to the law of $O$. For each individual $P$, use its finite conditional
response kernel specified below when assessing the MAR clause; arbitrary
null-state values do not affect that classification. The full-data mean $m(P)=P(Y=1)$ is an estimand on this
model. Its set of values over $\Theta_{a,b}$ is exactly
$$[b,b+1-a].$$
Consequently, without a MAR restriction, the mean is not identifiable when
$a<1$; it is identified as $b$ when $a=1$. If MAR also holds, then for $a>0$
the mean is $b/a$, while for $a=0$ it remains unidentified.

references.title: Lu Mao, Missing Data: Foundations and Methods, Chapter 1, §§1.6–1.7

items.title: MAR factorization and likelihood ignorability for the full-data parameter
items.statement:
Assume AC and the hypotheses and notation of
[[lem-observed-data-likelihood-under-response-model]]. Suppose the full-data
parameter and response-mechanism parameter range independently over the
nonempty Cartesian product $\Theta\times\Psi$, so the full-data law is
$P_\theta$ and the response kernel is $g_\psi$. For each pattern let $m_r$
denote the pattern reference selected in the lemma: $m_r=\kappa_r$ in
general, and one may take $m_r=\nu_r^{\mathrm{obs}}$ in the product-reference
special case. Let $Q_{\theta,r}$ be the law of $W_{\mathrm{obs}}(r)$ under
$P_\theta$, and choose a finite-valued nonnegative density representative
$q_{\theta,r}=dQ_{\theta,r}/dm_r$. Suppose MAR holds for every $\psi$ and $r$
with one measurable factor $h_{\psi,r}$ valid $P_\theta$-almost surely for
every $\theta$. Clipping this factor to $[0,1]$ preserves those
almost-sure identities, so take $0\le h_{\psi,r}(x)\le1$ for every $x$. Then
$$\ell_{\theta,\psi}(r,x)=h_{\psi,r}(x)q_{\theta,r}(x)$$
is a selected observed-record likelihood version relative to the disjoint
union reference $\lambda_O(A)=\sum_rm_r(\{x:(r,x)\in A\})$. In the
product-reference special case, the missing-coordinate integrals
$$\bar q_{\theta,r}(x)=\int p_\theta(x,z)\,\nu_r^{\mathrm{mis}}(dz),\qquad
\ell_{\theta,\psi}(r,x)=\int p_\theta(x,z)g_\psi(r\mid x,z)\,\nu_r^{\mathrm{mis}}(dz)$$
are density versions, and may be chosen in the displayed factorized form
after selecting finite-valued representatives.

For a fixed response parameter, if $h_{\psi,r}(x)>0$ and
$q_{\theta_2,r}(x)>0$, the factor cancels from the likelihood ratio in
$\theta$. Profiling over the same set $\Psi$ for each $\theta$ multiplies
$q_{\theta,r}(x)$ by the factor
$\sup_{\psi\in\Psi}h_{\psi,r}(x)$, which is independent of $\theta$; when
this factor is zero the observed record has zero likelihood for every
$\theta$. This licenses omission of the response factor for likelihood
inference about $\theta$ on its support. It does not license omission when the
target depends on $\psi$, or when the allowed parameter pairs are not a
Cartesian product.

references.title: Lu Mao, Missing Data: Foundations and Methods, Chapter 1, §1.4
National Research Council, The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials, Chapter 4, pp. 60–61

items.title: Death is not automatically a missing outcome
items.statement: If a quality-of-life score at time $t$ is defined only for participants alive at $t$ and $P(D=1)>0$ for death before $t$, then after-death values are not merely unrecorded components of a full-data random variable. An unconditional mean of that score over all enrolled participants is undefined until a different, scientifically meaningful target is specified.

references.title: Hernán and Robins, Causal Inference: What If, Chapter 8, §§8.4–8.5, and §12.6
National Research Council, The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials, Chapter 4, pp. 47–49

items.title: MCAR, MAR, MNAR, and indistinguishable observed laws
items.statement: For independent fair binary full-data components $X,Y$, response probabilities constant in $(X,Y)$ give an MCAR mechanism, probabilities depending only on the observed $X$ give a MAR mechanism, and probabilities depending on the unobserved $Y$ give an MNAR mechanism. Two explicit MNAR full-data laws can share response rate $a=1/2$ and observed success mass $b=1/4$ while their population means are $1/4$ and $3/4$.

references.title: Lu Mao, Missing Data: Foundations and Methods, Chapter 1, §§1.3–1.7
National Research Council, The Prevention and Treatment of Missing Data in Clinical Trials, Chapter 4, pp. 50–52
